artifacts.notes: Extent as the retrieving lane measured it: Complete uncorrected OCR of the 1568 Durandus-and-Beleth volume, used only to collate VI.128 against a second early printed edition; that collation is OCR against OCR, not against an image. Uncorrected optical recognition: a locating and searching layer, not a text of record. The volume also prints John Beleth's Summa, which is registered here as a separate work; these bytes are owned by the Durandus edition because that is what the lane read them for.
artifacts.rights_basis: The printing reproduced here was published before 1931 and is in the public domain in the United States: the repository's own rights reading, recorded at guidance/missals.md section 5 against Cornell's public-domain chart current at 1 January 2026, is that a work first published abroad before 1931 is in the public domain with no term running. The Internet Archive's optical character recognition of a public-domain printing is a mechanical transcription that adds no original authorship, is served without a copyright claim asserted over it, and carries none of the host's markup, navigation or apparatus. The bytes are retained here because guidance/sources.md makes retention the project-wide default and none of its three exemptions reaches this file: it may lawfully be republished, it is not restricted, and at 3.57 MB it is below the 5.88 MB that is the largest payload this library already retains.

edition.publication: An early printed composite volume: Durandus's Rationale divinorum officiorum with, as its own title page says, 'aliud Divinorum officiorum Rationale ab Ioanne Beletho Theologo Parisiensi' appended, each with its own index. Internet Archive item gri_33125009312923, from the Getty Research Institute.
edition.title: Rationale divinorum officiorum, with John Beleth's Rationale appended (1568)

alternate_titles: The Symbolism of Churches and Church Ornaments
work.author: William Durandus, bishop of Mende
work.description: Durandus of Mende's encyclopaedic commentary on the liturgy, in eight books. Book VI runs through the temporal year: chapter 128 is the Fourteenth Sunday after Pentecost and chapter 129 the Fifteenth. Durandus gives the Fourteenth the ten lepers and puts Matthew 6 and 'Primum quaerite' on the Fifteenth, with 'in quibusdam ecclesiis' attached to the Epistle, Gospel, Alleluia and Communion of the Fourteenth but not to its Introit or Offertory. John Beleth's Summa is printed under the same title Rationale divinorum officiorum and is a different work with its own record here; the alias is resolved so that a later search on the shared title does not merge them. The composition date is not established in this registration and is therefore not recorded.
work.title: Rationale divinorum officiorum
